findings.reason: a node told to find one remover across three runs will spend part of its budget on a run that never exhibited the defect, and the section's evidence base is two runs, not three.
findings.text: §13 states "Measured 2026-10-23 on three runs" ending "at launch with `worker did not spawn: CrewError: no live run '<run>'`", but the middle cited run `r-20261023T094330660097-plan-review-of-a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers` records no launch failure at all: its watch rows run `dispatched → queued → dispatched → working → queued → abandoned → discarded`, and its abandoned row's reason is the lane-allowance refusal "the lane's router grants 0 extra workers to session efd0ee8c…; admission headroom is 6" (`~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.events`), not a missing pointer

findings.reason: the records §13 names cannot name a remover, so §13 must instead point the node at where a launch failure does survive (the watch stream's `dispatched → abandoned launch-failed` transition and the pointer-side records the relaunch did not overwrite), or the node's required evidence is unobtainable by the route given.
findings.text: §13 directs the node to "each run directory's `supervisor.json`, `attempt-1-exit.json` and `tree-snapshot.json`" and to "the entries for those run ids in `admission-verdicts.jsonl`", but at HEAD each cited run directory holds a single completed attempt — `attempt-1-exit.json` for `r-20261023T140534758900-a-producer-off-the-fleet-node-gives-up-its-seat` reads `launched_at: 2026-10-23T15:02:17Z`, `ended_during: working`, `exit_code: 0`, which is the *successful relaunch* the section itself dates at 15:02:13Z, and the failing launch's own exit record was overwritten by it — while `admission-verdicts.jsonl` (428 lines, covering 2026-10-23T15:58:35Z–17:55:43Z) contains no entry naming any of the three run ids; the string `no live run` occurs zero times in both the run directories and the watch stream

findings.reason: if the remover resolves into `runs.py`, the coordinator's declared independence invites a concurrent dispatch that collides with §4 and §9 on a shared file; the section should fence the remover's home or declare the dependency it may acquire.
findings.text: §13 closes with "§13 writes no file another section writes, so it is independent of every other section", yet its write paths are `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` plus "the module the remover lives in if it is another one (named in the manifest)", and `reckon/crew/runs.py` is both part of the removal machinery §13 cites (`write_handover`/`clear_handover`, `list_live`) and a write path already assigned to §4 and §9

findings.reason: a done-when whose success path is unreachable on its recorded evidence makes the no-change report the node's only reachable outcome, so the section should either cite runs whose records show a remover or restate the gate around the failure it can actually prove.
findings.text: §13's done-when requires the manifest to "name the remover with record lines from at least two of the three runs", but as recorded none of those runs carries a remover, so the gate can only be met through the section's fallback ("the node reports that with the records it read and lands no product change")

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the per-run records §13 names are the successful relaunch's, not the failing launch's: each cited run's `attempt-1-exit.json` reads `exit_code: 0`, `ended_during: working`, and `admission-verdicts.jsonl` at HEAD holds no entry for any of the three cited run ids.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §13's done-when requires the manifest to "name the remover with record lines from at least two of the three runs", but no record it names carries a remover, so the only reachable outcome is the section's own fallback ("lands no product change").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §13 names the gate log and repository paths (`queue_admission.py`, the new test); no session scratchpad, node-local temporary path, or non-durable location for the evidence it asks for.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §13 introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose into symbols, files or comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — only two of the three runs §13 cites as measured instances of the launch failure actually record one, and none of the three records the pointer removal the section's mechanism asserts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 carries one deliverable (an admitted launch's pointer survives until its supervisor reads it) and one gate.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §13 declares itself independent of every other section, but leaves its write scope open to "the module the remover lives in if it is another one", and a plausible home for that remover (`reckon/crew/runs.py`) is a file this plan already assigns to §4 and §9.
